A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EditScore and EditReward-Bench research. All 21 pages of v1 and 30 pages of v3, including their appendices, are readable. Retained methods, experiments, figures, and derivations can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model evaluations, scoring ablations, Best-of-N experiments, and OmniGen2 RL results in Tables 2–5 and Figures 2–3, with qualitative examples in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds controlled RL comparisons, EmuEdit evaluation, annotation studies, efficiency measurements, hyperparameter ablations, and failure analyses.

M1.justification: v3 adds an EditScore variant based on Qwen3-VL-8B and evaluates RL using TempFlow-GRPO's temporal loss reweighting. The core generative reward formulation, SC/PQ combination, self-ensemble, and original Flow-GRPO procedure remain. The explicit arithmetic-mean equation clarifies the existing averaging strategy.

E1.justification: v3 adds EmuEdit as an explicitly out-of-distribution image-editing evaluation in Table 4. EditReward-Bench, GEdit-Bench, ImgEdit-Bench, and the original 13 editing subtasks remain. The new subtask breakdown analyzes existing coverage.

E2.justification: The UniPic2-SD3.5M-Kontext comparisons in v1 Table 5 are removed. v3 adds GPT-4.1 as a reward provider for the same OmniGen2 policy, alongside the retained Qwen reward controls. It also introduces Flow-GRPO versus TempFlow-GRPO comparisons and independent single-annotator controls for the discussion protocol, substantially expanding the comparison design.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 changes the reported annotation protocol from retaining completely agreeing dual ratings to expert-pair discussion and consensus; the PDFs do not establish that the benchmark was reannotated. Added experiments introduce sampling-step sweeps of 12/16/20, group-size sweeps of 8/12/16 at fixed global batch size, four-H100 cost normalization, and CLIP-I, CLIP-O, and DINO evaluation on EmuEdit.

E4.justification: v3 adds annotation-agreement validation, latency and throughput analysis, RL hyperparameter sensitivity studies, editor/optimizer generality checks, and a 13-subtask failure analysis with two illustrated cases. The original score-range, reasoning-format, and annotator-source analyses are retained. These additions substantially broaden the questions investigated.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, v3 Appendix D reports 10,000 paired bootstrap resamples, 95% confidence intervals, and one-sided p-values for reward-model and downstream RL comparisons. This adds test-set uncertainty analysis without establishing additional independent training runs. Several reported intervals and deltas conflict with the displayed point estimates in Tables 10–11.

E6.justification: The original Table 2 scores and OmniGen2 GEdit-Bench improvement from 6.28 to 6.68 are retained. v3 adds substantial results, including EmuEdit evaluation, Flux RL scores of 6.15 versus 6.87, TempFlow-GRPO's 7.21, and annotation, efficiency, and ablation outcomes. Added Table 13 contains unexplained alternative benchmark values: EditScore-72B Avg@4 overall accuracy is 0.751 there versus 0.763 in the retained Table 2.

T1.justification: The SDE derivation, score/vector-field relationship, transition distribution, and GRPO mathematics are retained from v1 Appendices B–C in v3 Appendices F–G, with renumbering. The newly displayed averaging equation formalizes the existing ensemble operation; no new theoretical result or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about the benchmark, specialized reward models, self-ensembling, Best-of-N selection, and stable online RL. Their scientific scope remains unchanged despite expanded supporting experiments.

C2.justification: New Appendix L identifies missed beautification improvements and excessive Semantic Consistency rewards for partially successful hybrid edits, linking these failures to visual capabilities and training-data limitations. v3 also adds interpretations of annotation discussion, hardware efficiency, group-size versus prompt-diversity tradeoffs, and generality across editors and optimizers.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents inference hosting on one, two, or four H100 GPUs, tensor parallelism, shared prefilling, and a 576-query reward stage taking approximately 18 seconds. Existing reward-model/RL training hyperparameters, training hardware, and full evaluation prompts are retained, moving from Appendices G–H to K and M.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Qwen3-VL, TempFlow-GRPO, and Tibshirani and Efron's bootstrap reference to support the new experiments and statistics. The original related-work discussion and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The annotation, efficiency, and RL-results passages receive localized rewrites and reorganization. Appendix references are updated and an ICLR publication header is added. Most of the introduction, related work, core method, conclusion, and retained appendix prose remain unchanged; the substantial scientific additions do not constitute a wholesale language rewrite.

P2.justification: Figure 2 becomes a two-panel FLOPs/latency comparison, the main RL table is redesigned, and numerous annotation, efficiency, statistical, hyperparameter, and subtask tables are added. Figure 7 introduces illustrated failure cases. Original annotation illustrations, qualitative examples, and interface screenshots are retained with layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important gaps through fixed-editor reward comparisons, OOD/generalization tests, efficiency measurements, and explicit failure analysis. However, Tables 2 and 13 give unexplained conflicting benchmark scores, Tables 10–11 contain interval/delta inconsistencies, and Table 4 claims consistent superiority over GPT-4.1 despite reporting GEdit overall scores of 6.68 versus 6.73 for EditScore-7B and GPT-4.1. These problems affect central quantitative evidence, preventing a reliable net quality judgment despite the useful additions.
